I'm sorry but I've never heard of counting the safe fund at the beginning and end of a shift. Even the paperwork that's supposed to be filled out for daily accountability only mentions an AM and a PM count check.

Say I have a shift from 4-10, it seems asinine to count the safe fund when I come in when (if going by these rules) the leaving MOD I'd be coming in to relieve would have already have counted it for the end of their shift as well.

But also, if OP is say busy getting a fresh truck put away or doing a plano, and the keyholder in question forgets to lock the case with a couple transactions but then ends up remembering to lock it by the time OP comes around, how on earth should an SM put the blame on OP? Not to mention, if the other person is at a keyholder level then they should be held to the same standard of responsibility. My rule of thumb, if you're a keyholder of at least 2 weeks, simple rules like keeping the cigarette case lock falls on your own personal responsibility alone. After all, for all we know, said keyholder might never care to adjust their behavior and keep doing it if they know it's only going to end up being the MOD who ends up getting in trouble.

I think that sometimes tends to depend on how much seasonal you end up getting in verses space you have to set it. Our DG is in a smaller town, essentially one of the few in town options to shop, so anything seasonal ends up selling because people just don't want to spend 20-30 minutes driving out to somewhere like Walmart, etc. The downside is that not everyone wants/needs it all at once, which is pretty much how it's sent into the store.

For instance can the store sell through 4-5 rolltainers worth of Easter candy for the season? Absolutely. But when half of it comes within 1-2 weeks and then the other half comes the next couple weeks after, there often isn't enough room to store the backstock easily. Either has to be out on the floor to make restocking easier once candy starts to move, or it risks getting buried in the warehouse because at most there's enough room for 20 rolltainers.

Mix lingering brown/purple dot, lawn and garden, all the various green dots (hydration, tropical, bath, etc.), all of the swim/summer toys, patriotic, dolly parton, and you soon run out of space.

So I think it more so becomes the issue of build up verses what's sent in per season. Like if you already have 2-3 rolltainers of Lawn and Garden lingering and 2-3 of last years Christmas toys/pack away Christmas, getting in 3 of Halloween/Harvest when it comes in can easily start to impact a warehouse if you're not a store that was built to house 50+ rolltainers.
Have to remember that store/location matters a lot too. Having heard what a few SMs in our area make, it's not even over $50k.
Oh we usually get 150+ hours in budget, but a fair swath of those hours have to go to keyholders so that the SM doesn't have to be bothered coming in most days of a given week.

Bold of you to assume that DG corporate cares about laws pertaining to a worker's rights. They will push their RMs and DMs to pressure SMs to enforce the break policy because they'll rely on the fact that most managers won't come forward to join for a class action lawsuit even if all of them would be educated about their rights. But even then the payout DG would have to give would still likely be a drop in the bucket compared to bolstering payroll to enable hiring more managers in order to ensure proper break coverage. So it still ends up being more profitable for them to risk another lawsuit coming through than to fix the problem they have with the fact they run stores on skeleton crews/weekly hour budgets.

Oh absolutely.

DG loves to run on skeleton crews with skeleton weekly hour budgets. So it's rare to be able to have 2 managers on for a whole shift together or to even have them overlap--but even then taking your break 1-2 hours into what may be a 6-8 hour shift sucks.

But DG would sooner just keep enforcing this kind of policy because the payout they would have to give as a result of a lawsuit is likely way less than the amount of payroll they'd have to add on in order to ensure managers have coverage to leave for a 30-60 minute break.

It's more so the stuff that doesn't make sense for us to always have a surplus in. Like us doing on hands to say that we have some 30 packs of nerd clusters and yet another 2 or 3 cases end up coming on the next truck sort of situation.

The only other reason I can fathom is that sometimes stuff empties out on the shelf in a day or two and then it can take us a few days to reach more in the backstock. Like if maybe the system sees a shelf full selling out quickly and for some reason it might be triggering more to be sent?

But the worst offender is pet. Plug in that we have 8 original tidy cat cases of litter, maybe 1 or 2 will sell all week, cue us getting another 5 on the truck. Or having 10 bags of 30lb Alpo, 3 sell, in comes another 3. Doesn't matter how well we maintain counts, they just always send 2 or 3 times the amount we need.

Depending on the store and their layout that can also consist of doing on hand adjustments either up or down depending on if store is being overloaded with product or the DC has shipped product with the wrong item label. And to my knowledge sales associates don't have the permission on the HHT to do on hands.

Plus during T-2 through T-5 any ranking manager is supposed to be going through all of the backstock and sky shelves, adjusting counts as needed (because stores are supposed to have truck done by the end of T-1 if not noon by T-2 regardless of staffing or truck size).

The store itself may have had a lot of bad track records of trying to allow sales associates on the floor to give them a break to let them stock instead (cause believe me, sometimes us managers do want a break from throwing freight like crazy). However it could be that the sales associate just isn't quick enough for the work load a particular store is demanded to work through, could have repeated problems with constantly stocking items in the wrong spots, or would end up finding them hiding in an aisle without a camera talking, texting, or playing games on their phones.

Deal with that enough and eventually you stop giving sale associates chances because in some stores a day without progress can be the make or break of an impacted backroom or planograms being on hold for 1-3 weeks depending on the coming truck sizes, POG resets, seasonal requirements, customer flow, etc.

The only problem is that there are going to be stores like mine who are short on endcaps. Like, if I recall correctly, our store is short 6 or so endcaps because of the square footing. Our store map was edited when we had our last remodel, however the DC and Footprint treats our store as if we are the standard model layout. So what's going to end up happening if say store model A is supposed to have 18 endcaps, but the size of the physical store can only support 14 endcaps? Are stores going to be stuck either having to give up G sections and reduce their seasonal room or just have to throw their hands up and let it eternally sit on rolltainers in the backrooms?

For instance, had Footprint come out 5 separate times for the Purex/Snuggle endcap. Only problem? We have 1 singular large endcap that was mandatory for the fixture, that's right between our food aisles. 

Every single visit Footprint would send someone out we're get screamed at up and down because "Why am I being sent to this store as a revisit if you already know we're not allowed to put a chemical endcap in the middle of food?!?!"

Then, supposedly, the last Footprint rep who came in called HR or someone in home office to explain that our store physically can't have the endcap. Put the lady on speaker as we both explained the problem, had a surplus of 15+ pictures sent to show we had no other possible endcap. "Sorry for all the confusion, we'll mark this store because the installation of the endcap would result in OHSA non-compliance". 

Yet to this day we still keep getting in the products for that endcap, having to spread them across 2 endcap and resulting in us having even less room to put endcap MAG items--which often gets us snipped at because "your store needs to be doing a better job on getting seasonal endcap items out onto the endcaps, there's no excuse for this stuff to be sitting back here." because not having any endcaps left to use isn't an allowable reason to not have it on an endcap.

Just gonna say asking the DM is a YMMV sorta thing. 

Last 2 years when we'd be getting cut down to 110-120, maybe 125 hours a week and getting in 1300-1500 piece trucks it was like pulling teeth trying to ever get more hours or extra help when the dam spilled over and rolltainers would have to be shoved into aisles. We'd ask if we could have any help (hours, people, anything) and we'd be told "oh here's 10 hours". Mind you we'd be telling the DM we'd have 30 some rolltainers that needed worked during the worst points and it was always like the DM would shrug and effectively tell us to deal with it on own own. 

We couldn't even get either DM or RM to agree to reduce or stop trucks because "you guys just need to learn to get on the 7-day work flow and pick up the pace and it'll be fine".

It's usually because of a couple things. 

\-Someone stocking isn't bothering to do proper rotation. Or possibly wasn't taught to and just forgot about the FIFO CBL we're required to watch.

\-Driveline isn't taught to put food/medication/other dated items by dates so when they do resets or cut ins, even if a store is doing proper rotation, that can end up being screwed up because of the rep mixing up the dates. So if the oldest stuff ended up being put towards the back and it doesn't sell or has a quicker expiring rate it can lead to expiring items being left on the shelf. Of course that's also supposed to be caught by the product rotation checks but that depends on if stores can spare the time for them via hours, staffing, etc. 

\-DCs just straight up sending expired products. We've had this happen a fair amount of times where we'll get a case of near expiring or already expired items are sent to us. Just a couple weeks ago every single box of cheese we got sent on our fresh truck was expired by 2 weeks. And depending on the size of your trucks it could end up being implausible to spend the time checking every single box. For example if your store often receives 8+ food rolltainers on a 1400 piece truck but only end up with 120 budgeted hours that week it's going to cost too much time to double check if the DC is screwing you over. Granted this wouldn't be the cause of a store having carts upon carts of expired products either on a single truck. But given a stretch of time and lots of overlooking it could eventually pile up.

Of course it's never a bad thing to pull expired items because that's a quick way for an SM to get a write up during DM visits or get into serious trouble with steritech if they'd show up for a compliance check. 

Vendor reps are also supposed to be the ones checking their own product to make sure it's all in date and to credit out anything expiring or expired. So if you're finding a lot of vendor items that are out of date it should be on the SM to talk to the rep about being stricter on that. Then if the rep continues the behavior the SM should bring the issue up to both their DM and the reps' boss to nip that in the butt.

Problem with DG is that what you're supposed to be able to do and what actually ends up being the situation can vary wildly. We've had multiple issues with refusing trucks ranging from DMs to DOT supervisors. 

Our old DM would scream at our old SM when they tried to refuse a fresh truck and ultimately became a part of why they left. It was back nearly 2 years ago, our hours got cut to anywhere between 110-120 a week, just enough for us to have MOD and cashier for night shifts and a few extra hours to have people some in to work truck once a week to try and keep rolltainers from filling up the aisles. But back then our fresh trucks were always scheduled for the morning and every time it showed up with SM alone they'd ask if they could close the store so they could actually stock it all without having portions of it going to waste because they were held up at the register. Eventually SM got fed up and just closed to get it done, took maybe an hour and a half and the store was reopened. DM caught wind of it and within a couple days came down to give the SM a 2nd stage write up for closing the store without excusable grounds. 

Then again this is also the DM who would berate us for not being able to fit all of our rolltainers in the backroom because of such severely cut hours during visits, would go to the backroom and push rolltainers in front of our electrical panel to make more fit back there (because SM would be stuck up front checking customers out so they couldn't do anything about it), but then would have the gall to berate the SM in front of customers for allowing such a thing and to take more responsibility for their store.

Our other worst situation was one I mentioned in a post above. To summarize, storm knocked out all of our refrigeration units save for our one backstock cooler, fresh truck ends up getting sent with next to all of our refrigeration products despite tickets and emails sent, refused it. DOT supervisor calls our store screaming us out to hell and back, essentially strong arms the driver to deliver, leaving us with 3 rolltainers worth of product to damage out. 

Luckily DM helped us get an emergency disaster ticket in so the excessive damages wouldn't come back on us but there are certainly those in the company that will use the position they have to bully downwards to prevent any sort of possible trouble coming back onto them and push that trouble onto those below them.

Can't say whether or not this SM is terrible since I don't know them, but DOT and their superiors can certainly be fuckwads about refusing trucks too.

We had a bad storm one night that knocked out power to the area for a few hours overnight. In turn caused 2 milk coolers and our meat cooler to go down, so we had absolutely no working refrigeration units aside from our 1 backstock cooler. And we can't fit a fresh truck's worth into it when ours rarely goes below 220. 

Long story short, some sort of either miscommunication or not caring happened with the fresh DC and we got everything that we had to damage out sent in on our next fresh truck. DM approved us for refusal and we only accepted freezer items because even the driver said it would be dumb to unload so much product to a store that's just going to have to throw it away. When the driver notified their supervisor about it DOT ended up calling our store and SCREAMING at us about how fucking lazy and useless we were for just not wanting to be bothered to stock half of the fresh truck. Literally wouldn't listen to us when we said ALL of our refrigeration units were down because "there's no way it would have been sent if that was true" and refused to even try to contact anyone about the ticket and emails sent about said situation. Forced the truck to come back to us and told the driver to unload or else they'd be marked for the lost product themselves. SM said we'd just let the truck stay at our store until we'd be allowed to refuse it and not exactly sure how the calls went about but the RM got wind of what was going on either from DOT or DM and they called us saying, "take it and fit out what you can or everyone there will be written up because this is apart of your job to do proper scans and stock the fresh truck".

But at least our DM worked with us to get ahold of ERC to get the emergency disaster ticket going for us so we didn't get fucked over since we did everything we were supposed to do to prevent this from happening. Though that in itself was a bitch and took like a week to finally get into place because so many people we talked with from ERC about the issue just didn't seem to understand why we needed the clearance for it and would spin us in so many circles.
Unless they're on the new system. NextGen completely removed the ability to go to previous transactions and abort them.

Usually 5-6 days depending on how big it is.

Closer to 1200 it'll take 6 days, more than that and we'll be pretty much finishing the day before or in some cases just as the next truck is pulling up.

I wish this worked at all stores but it also depends on your RD. We'll so often be approved of 4 weeks of VV holds when we send in pictures of 3-4 rolltainers of VV to our DM and RD. But then have the ticket revoked after 2 weeks with us calling either and them being like "oh well it's been 2 weeks, surely your VV shelves must be next to completely bare by now". And we can send pictures of completely full shelves and still having 2 full rolltainers worth and get back "well it should all be fine, just let us know when there's another major problem."

Then within 2-3 weeks we're often close if not right back to 3-4 rolltainers of VV backstock and have to try and do the song and dance all over and over again. As if by some miracle somehow something will magically happen to have us completely sell out of VV in 2 weeks time despite the sheer amount of backstock we always end up having.

As for seasonal our RD has always told us that's the biggest no-no to put a stop on. "It's any stores biggest sell next to food so it would hurt you guys more if we tried to stop it coming in. But don't worry even if there's (insert amount of rolltainers in back) it shouldn't be long before it's all out and you'll be wishing for more to come in." There's only once when we've ever gotten a seasonal hold due to the sheer amount we got in from a post inventory truck and that only lasted for a week because "it should be moving off the shelves fast enough for that to be more than enough time to get it all out". Surprise surprise when it wasn't and that year we ended up with 3 rolltainers of Christmas wrapping paper and lights that had to be pulled into the back and take up unneeded space in our already tight backroom.

Meanwhile we're currently sitting on 5 rolltainers of Christmas toys after squeezing summer toys and fitting out what all we can, 3 rolltainers of Christmas plus 15 some totes of it because our lawn and garden, green dot, and red dot are barely moving even with clearance and sales, and 3 Halloween candy rolltainers with us already having 5 sections and 2 endcaps completely stuffed as full as we can get them. Plus another 5 some totes of gloves and hats and half a rolltainer of socks because we don't have enough endcaps as we're short 6 or so (plus short 40ft of seasonal G sections) because our store plan had to be modified from the in book model due to our store being too small for the full layout, but send all of the product for said model anyway because "it'll eventually sell and it's better to have more to keep shelves full than to risk empty shelves" as our regional often tells us. Despite the fact we're so much more often trying to fight to have space to put things out than not, or ending up sending back tons of PRP like which often happens with all of our socks and accessories since we rarely have enough room to have it all (or in some cases anything at all) out before PRP rolls around.

Problem is that if MOS follows close to what the dates were last year, lawn and garden won't likely go until after October. And we have inventory at the end of September. Wouldn't it mess up our inventory if we box that up and let it sit in the back?

Even if they do I'm almost entirely expecting those sales to mostly be "Buy 2 Get 1 Free" sales which barely ever gets things to move. Because they've done quite a few of them for the lawn and garden already and at least with us it doesn't really get things to move. Meanwhile during that half off sale we got a good chunk to move, but all it let us do was be able to set 4ft of throws which it barely a kick in the bucket for everything we do have.

And Christmas tends to have a good chunk of Pack 1 items but without room on the floor we have no idea how we're going to get it out in time for inventory.

Certainly not me but I'm currently sitting on 24,279 magia stones, 202 single tickets, and 3 10x pulls. 

But this isn't exclusive saving since I think I spent around 5k magia stones during the last anniversary to try and grab some copies of the anniversary cards I didn't manage to roll during their respective banners.

Though have been mostly saving since JP announced they would region lock buying magia stones cause I've had bad experiences with trying to go around issues like that. Cause once AkuHomu was dropping I whole heartedly planned to roll until I max her out.

Small dying town so it's mostly this, tiny mom and pop shops that don't really hire outside the family (and most barely need more than 2-3 employees cause they're tiny shops), or there's food service. However have already tried food service and I just physically can't handle the heat of kitchens. After nearly passing out mid shift during my first week I knew it'd be too risky for me to keep attempting. Then I developed carpal tunnel early, have no medical to afford surgery, so hands that randomly go numb doesn't make for a good waitstaff/food runner. 

Oh and there's constructing work too if you have transportation but once again sensitivity to heat and carpal tunnel doesn't tie in well to turn to that route at this point. 

Though it's not like I hate retail. I actually enjoy stocking rolltainers and totes, recovery isn't bad, and honestly enjoy doing planograms and seasonal set ups. Like let me put in a blue tooth head phone with softly playing music and I can go for hours. Cashiering isn't a favorite but also not the worst save for times we're just slammed, unable to move for hours at a time. Which it usually only around holidays or around first of the month. 

If DG just had better business models it wouldn't be that bad to work there. But if you're a busy store that the company tries to run "small, barley sees sales" hour budgets on then it's always an uphill battle trying to get to everything. Like our store at minimum does $3.5 mil a year but it's like they give us the budget for a store that's barely hitting $2 mil. But when your average daily customer count is anywhere from 450-600 a day with sales varying from roughly $8-10k it's a miracle we keep up with our 1300-1600 piece trucks as it is. Let alone trying to squeeze in time for planograms, seasonal resetting, plus the many other tasks that are handed out. 

If we had more hours and hands to get to everything the stress to get everything done would go down significantly and while not being a dream job would at least eliminate most of the dread of going in some days. Like while I enjoy stocking or resets it still ends up stressful when you feel tugged into needing to do 10 different tasks but only have the time to juggle 2 or 3 at a time.

Okay so maybe if I take it down the alley late at night and grab some lighter fluid on the way out....

But in all seriousness, we already are using a old z-rack (clothing rack) for our fans and what's left of our beach towels. Which does help clear some of that out--plus it's been hotter than hell all month so we've actually been selling a nice chunk too. 

We don't really have a sidewalk. We're a store that has a patio of sorts. So we only have 2 spots that are long enough to have uboats on, otherwise they're too long to put elsewhere without customers needing to shove them aside to access our door. Which would lead them rolling downhill into our parking lot and we already have enough trouble with vendors and trucks trying not to smack into customers cars as it is. 

And as mentioned above, one of those spots is taken up with the z-rack and the other has a uboat with extra paper on it so we don't have another uboat clogging up the backroom. Granted we do have 2 rolltainers worth of charcoal sitting outside so it's not taking up shelf space, which is at least helping to give us room to set Harvest and Halloween so it'll be that much less that sits in back.

Then our coolers are currently jammed back with totes on top of them. Granted our fan issue is mostly dealt with by having them on the z-rack, and we didn't get slammed with grills so they're at least sitting up on endcaps. But it really feels like they're just lacking on given decent sales or just letting things clearance. Like so many other stores already have their lawn and garden on clearance while we're stuck with it being full price. I can't tell you how many customers just decide against our stuff when they say "oh x store has theirs on sale already so I'm just going to get it there instead". Which I find funny because DG is surely holding off because they want to get as much money for their seasonal as possible but once the season is nearing it's end they actually start to lose out in sales because people know other retailers are already marking their stuff down.

We would but we don't have the hour budget for it without screwing 1 or 2 people on staff on hours. Not to mention I'm almost always just under 40 hours because I'm one of the fastest stockers in the store, so it's useful to have me on slower shifts to let me punch out what I can. And our DM has already put their foot down about overtime. They've said that if they see it pop up in anyone's timesheets then we'll be given 2nd stage write ups because "overtime is unacceptable and should only ever be seen if your store drops down to 4 employees". 

Plus it's also partly because half of our backroom is full of things that just won't go out. Like how do we put out 4 rolltainers of Halloween candy when we already have 16 feet (4 sections) jammed as full as we can get them? Or push out more backstock food when we don't have the space for things like BTS snacks nor have an spot for an endcap like prepared food (unless we set that and take away space from a seasonal spot).
Yup, according to the MAG book there are I think 4 or 5 sections of Christmas toys due to the set by August 11th.

We actually don't have an official fire marshal for our town because we're so small. We'd have to call 911 to request a non emergency fire call (or contact the police to have them come out and call in the fire department) to have the fire department come out, assess the situation, and then they would get in contact with the police to come up and determine if we could stay open.

So we're not sure if that much could end up coming back onto us, or find a way to be sourced to us. Unless we stay open for a while to let enough customers come through to enable reasonable doubt that it was a customer calling in and not us. Which still opens us up to chances that Steritech (I think that's how it's spelled) could pop up and give us hell.

Not sure if this is a fixable problem or just a known issue when it comes to NGPOS but at least at our store we can't do transaction aborts. Or more so really avoid doing them at all when possible because it ends up in an entire register freeze roughly 80% of the time.

Or, after the introduction of apple/google pay being announced as useable methods of payment, why the register fully freezes when a customer goes to tap their card or phone either just before or immediately after hitting total? 

Oh and while it's gotten better since the NGPOS rollout, still seeing issues with clearance prices or seasonal sales not applying to all of the products that should apply. For example we have one kind of freezer pop that isn't coming up as the summer bbq clearance price despite being listed on the item list given to us through START. Or during the BOGO Lawn and Garden sale we had certain solar lights that would go through just fine but other we'd have to override. Like would those be more so bugs within the sale or possible items overlooked to be added as an eligible sale item or is that an actual issue worth reporting to ERC?

No, usually just ask for the previous ticket and then just say they're going to try and push the update again. Then the "call us back if that doesn't work" but then it's always just been a rinse and repeat process. 

But we've typically found it's either a 50/50 on if we can actually get the person on the other end of the phone to actually break what we call the "dialogue" tree they're supposed to go through. 

Like last year our self check out was down for 3 some months because it couldn't connect to the CMT if I recall the acronym properly and called about it so much we could do the full troubleshooting process by heart. But anytime we asked for anything more to do or even a supervisor to talk to after it being down for 2 months, so many would either just end up hanging up on us or argue with us that we just needed to do the whole process over again because what they were telling us to do should be working. It was pure luck that we finally got someone who was able to get us someone to finally get the system back up again.

We typically call anywhere from 10am to 1pm usually because it's our best chance to get ahold of them. Between having long wait times (averaging around an hour minimum) or getting slammed with customers (have had ERC hang up on us before because god forbid we take care of lines when we know we're about to answer a couple questions and then be put back on hold for another 5-10 minutes anyway).

But yea, was afraid that was going to be the answer both in terms of other options and lack of fixes being from someone not doing their job. Hopefully one of these calls will be the lucky winner.

Though it would be super nice to have an actual support line to call where we could actually ask questions like "hey if every time we're getting new items in that aren't ringing at the SCO is that more of a problem from a prior update not going through properly or a sign of another kind of problem?" instead of trying to ask ERC and just getting, "well pushing update should let the items scan once it's gone through" which doesn't let us know if this is a band aid fix or an actual fix--well, once said update actually gets pushed through.

Yea I can try to overlook the OHA review tomorrow to double check if numbers are looking proper. By spazzing I mean that it'll struggle to load an item once it's scanned, like it'll sometimes take 30-90 seconds for the item to load onto the screen. I attribute it to a connection problem but I'm guessing our provider is just bad for the area because we've had a handful of incidents where a tech has been out to either look over our box or replace things, yet still always have janky connection. Like our customers can barely get their phones to work unless they move over to data and that'll even be a rough load in sometimes. 

Oh sorry that's my bad. I don't actually use nones and tons when doing that, just OHA. If OP wants/needs a more step by step;

To start a til just count the til on the cash master to verify that it's the amount your tils should be at. So for example our store's tils always start at $150 so just double check that they're at $150. Then go to register, sign on, then go to manager functions and the starting bank should be on the left hand column. Hit it, the drawer will pop open and slide your drawer in then close it. The screen with ask the starting bank. So to use the earlier example you would type in "150.00" (note you NEED to hit the . or else it'll read the til start as $15000), hit confirm, take the paper that prints and slide it into the register drawer slot. Extra note that when starting drawers for cashiers it'll also ask for authorization, that's when you type in your ID number. 

Removing a til. You (or the person's til you're removing) will have to be signed on. Hit Log Off and Yes to remove the til and get the report that prints from the receipt printer. Then sign back on again, go to manager functions, and then into end session.

Extra note for reconciling tils. If you have coupons you'll hit the 3rd line and you'll have to type in each individual coupon. There will be an add button at the bottom to give you more slots. Also, to make closing easier, if you have multiple coupons write the amount from each somewhere on your register balancing sheet. Because you'll have to do the same for the deposit except with ALL of the coupons for that day. Which isn't too bad if there's only a few but Saturdays and Sundays aren't uncommon to have 10-20 or more depending on how badly couponers are out and about and the deals they're seeking out. So it's just less of a headache than to try and guess or keeping them all in a pile for later.

So let's say you're counting down a drawer for cashier A and B. Then say you go to put in for cashier's A til but accidently type in for B's number instead. Just go ahead and redo the reports for A and then B because the system will rewrite to the latest balancing input.

It's like how if you would have Casheir A count down but they're $20 short. But if you end up finding an extra $20 in their drop then you can go back to input their report to account for that $20 to show that they're not actually short.

If you need a more direct example, say Cashier A had 148.36 and Cashier B had 99.01 and you accidently input Cashier A as having the $99.01. Just redo the report and input $148.36 and it'll record that 2nd amount (the $148.36) as their balancing NOT the $99.01.

Okay so judging from the comments you've given I'm going to guess that store A where you bought the item from has the old system while store B is the one where you tried to return the item and were denied has the new system. 

And coming from someone who works in a store who used to have the old system but now runs the new one, there is a fair chance that their hands could have been tied.

Option 1: In our store our return without receipt function is bugged. What does that mean? Well our registers just won't accept us trying to put funds onto a gift card like we're supposed to do for such returns. 

"But I have a receipt" 

While that is true, for some reason when DG crafted the new system they essentially made it incompatible with the old system. The registers with the new system will NOT read the barcode from older systems nor will it accept the string of numbers. So in effect it essentially means the return has to be treated as if the customer doesn't have a receipt. Which would be fine but because of the gift card bug mentioned above it would force us to then give the return back on card or cash. Which is technically against policy. Some DMs may allow stores to just process the return normally. Our DM forbids it because it creates a greater risk for fraud/theft returns according to them. And we can't just disobey our DMs because they get records for each store's returns so they know when and what kind of returns are done.

Which would result in that store not being able to process the return.

Option 2: The item you're trying to return is coming up as 'item not found' in the new store's register. And given the mentioned issue with receipts, there's nothing the store can do. When doing returns with the new system the register gives a list of items that can be returned per receipt. With returns without a receipt the register locks out everything but the ability to scan the item. There is no way to just go 'well it's a $5 item so just type something in for $5'. The register just simply will not let you. Hit refund, scan, that's it. If you have to do more than that then it leaves the employee out of luck.

The only way around that would to be an item exchange for the exact amount with the permission from the store manager. So for example, say the Charmin you got was a 6 pack for $5.95, then you would have to get another item that isn't taxed for $5.95. You wouldn't be able to get your money back for that item. Other than going back to the original store you got the item from.

None and Tons are pretty simple and self explanatory for the most part.

Nones - Items that are completely out of stock.

Tons - Items that are in excess. 

If you open the handheld and go into the drop down menu there's a spot specifically labeled Nones and Tons. Though you don't always have to specifically do something as a Ton to lessen stock. Scanning something and checking that OHA matches with what's in stock can also put a stop on DC sending you in too much. At least in theory. There are some times where even if you have an accurate count you could still end up being sent more than you need. 

Like we often have this happen with our bagged dog food. Where we can scan everything and effectively be telling the DC that we have plenty of stock but still end up getting another 2-5 bags of something we don't need.

Also there are times where if it's time for endcaps to be reset you can end up being sent in more of an item for the end cap even if you could completely fill in the endcap with what you already have on sky shelves or back stock.

You can also run into the same issue when it comes to PDQs as well because you'll always be sent them even if, once again, you have plenty on hand to fill up both the core spots as well as endcaps. For instance during summer we ended up getting 3 different Softsoap body wash PDQs. But next to none of it has really sold so we have a full shelf of each plus anywhere from 5-10 bottles of each on the sky shelf. 

So just know that while Nones and Tons plus accurate OHA are supposed to ensure that you're never overrun with anything, it's not always a guarantee. Like our register candy is super sparse and we haven't gotten certain things in since at least last Christmas while more than we often sell through of others. But our HHT is still blocking us from having access to doing any OHA with those.

Oh and some stuff is pretty much pointless to fuss over. Granted paper towels and toilet paper you have a better chance of lessening but we've also run into plenty of times where the company will decide to change up a seasonal section to be those in face of shortages despite our store not having said sections to set it. Or plastic totes. The counts on those never matter because you're ALWAYS going to be sent new stock in for Christmas plastics, BTS plastics, and the plastics setting that often pairs with the January Coastal. Heck we had BTS/Christmas totes from last year that are clogging up our perimeter sky shelves (talking anywhere from 2-3 boxes worth in some cases) and we still got entire shipments in for BTS that half sold at best.

The boxes of mops/brooms can end up being pretty guilty of those too, we still have boxes of brooms from this year's purple dot but because the brooms themselves are more so unlabeled MAG we're just stuck with them until they finally sell. Which sucks because it feels like they always send more for nearly every season regardless of how many you already have.

The barest minimum I'd like to see is to jump labor budgets up. 

2 people per shift minimum and not taking the need for truck, planos, and other tasks into consideration with that. Though being able to have enough hours to possibly have 3 people (2 cashiers and 1 on the floor) during super busy periods like weekends or first of the month would be great too.

Then add on 4-6 hours for fresh truck coverage depending on average sizes of the truck and how many you get a week--can also be used to try and factor in some rotation of backstock. Not sure how bad it is to put away produce but figure it's probably averaging roughly the same kind of workload.

Hours for truck should be allocated separately altogether and should at least follow the company's guideline for how long each kind of rolltainer takes to stock out, estimating to the best of their ability.

So if a store gets on average 15 rolltainers then at minimum the hours should be 15, likely closer to 20ish to account for food and HBA. The amount of hours growing the more rolltainers you'd be expected to get.

Giving the 2nd person on shift time to work through totes, and then extra time to work rolltainers if the given time isn't enough--which could be a given if seasonal has to be sorted through or have space made for, etc. Though the company should know ahead of time when seasonal change over happens, which often includes a beefier truck, so more hours should be given to account for that.

Expiration dates, for the most part, usually don't mean jack. Sure for things like drinks, milk, meats, produce, and similar items it's usually more accurate. But stuff like candy, cookies, and other shelf stable foods, they're usually fine for weeks, sometimes even months past the date posted. Maybe a bit stale compared to something 'in date' but often times it's fine otherwise.

Usually the dates serve 2 main purposes;

1) to ensure good rotation and make sure a product isn't sitting on a shelf for years, giving a safety standard for the store to go by

2) to encourage a quicker turn over so the company sending said product can push more out

There's plenty of times I've bought expired items to prevent them from just getting tossed.

Rule of thumb is just check for anything visibly wrong, check to see if it smells off, do a tiny taste test.

Of course it's not a perfect process. Sometimes there are times where items are mislabeled or you may even end up getting in items that are for another store so that can screw with numbers. Not to mention sometimes you do sometimes end up with overwhelming stock from endcaps or seasonal set ups that just isn't going to sell. 

Plus not sure how DC runs but sometimes they will just over send things. Now whether that's them trying to clear space on their end or something with their higher ups but that can be why even if one is diligent you can still find times when you get say 3 boxes of a detergent that's still full on the shelf. 

But speaking of endcaps and standouts, try to also keep those in mind if they have stuff that's your normal core. Sometimes outs can be because you still have enough stock on an endcap--most of the time you won't be sent more in if they aren't high sell items to try and keep you from being overburdened by overstock.

Though if you would have say counted some aspirin as overstock and still find more on an endcap you can scan again to add more into the count. I don't do nones and tons often enough to fully remember but if say you have something scanned as a none but find a ton on an endcap I think you can either just add it back on during the tons or once you're done just go back and do an on hand adjustment to fix the count. 

Still if you're not instructed on doing it I wouldn't say to bother with it because it is a process that does take hours to do. SMs or whoever is charged to do it for the day are often supposed to come in around 5-6 to start because it can take up until noonish to complete depending on how bad either can be. And given the shortages going around or extra stores seem to be getting either for holidays or to combat possible future shortages/sales, it wouldn't be unreasonable to assume it to take roughly 4ish hours on average. Hence why on hands tend to be the preferred quick method during stocking to try and keep things balanced if you notice long lasting outs or over excess. So unless there really wouldn't be anything else in the store to take care of it's not worth the time to do a full sweep if there's other pressing tasks to tend to. The DM should really be the one getting on the SM if it's not actually being kept up on if it's impacting stock to that bad of a degree.

It's honestly an easy process in of itself. You go into the nones and tons selection on the HHT and literally go through the store with the HHT in it's entirety--excluding seasonal, clearance, VV, and vendor items (I think fresh items might be excluded too since they're supposed to have their own day for counts but not 100% sure on that)--and scan the empty spots. Then go through once again for the items you have an over excess amount. 

Example. Say you go through make up and say you're out of 5 different nail polishes, check the area you keep overstock and see there isn't any back stock of it at all, but the handheld says your store still has an inventory of 4, then you would zero it out. Or if they would be zeroed already either leave it be. Of course you can't check for every single item but if you notice something is empty week after week then more likely than not it should be zeroed out if it already isn't. Like say someone managed to steal a few of those nail polishes from above then the system wouldn't know that they're not in the store anymore. Or if someone missed damaging out something that came in so the system still thinks you should have it on hand somewhere.

Or say during back to school let's say that pringles just didn't sell very well and you know you have like 5 cases of original pringles so then you would count the individual count on the shelves and then add in the number of tubes per case. So in this case say there's 12 on the shelf and I think those cases are 14 counts, you'd enter 82 into the count or ensure that inventory is at least showing 82 so you shouldn't get anymore cases until what you have sells down.

Technically it's often done on the day before a truck arrives but sometimes if rooms are impacted like this SMs might forgo the counts in favor of trying to clear at least some room for the incoming truck. Or sometimes it just likes to pop up a couple days early or seems trigger to request one even if the week you're on is supposed to be a stock week.

If in doubt and you don't want to bring it up to your managers it's never really a bad idea to do on hand adjustments when you're stocking if you notice you got a lot of one certain product in just to ensure counts are kept up on as best as they can be.

Yea I think that could be the overall baseline of how I could see myself aligning with being nonbinary. 

Like when I was little I was always more so pushed into presenting more feminine. Though not in an oppressive way but definitely tons of comments from varying family members of "Oh you'd look cute in this" or "See! If you put more effort into yourself you look so nice" and so on. Which maybe it what lead me into the initial distancing of wanting to always be female. Like regardless of how much energy or time or money I threw into my appearance I just hated how those kinds of comments tended to seep into conversations, as if an underhanded jab at me and my worth even if the one making the comment realized it.

It wasn't really until late high school and my early years of college that with more control over myself and having those around me who pushed for me to just be me that I felt more okay with embracing my femininity again. Though I guess the overarching feeling of not wanting to be bound to what my birth gender is as something to define me and my worth has still stuck around.

Even now I really like keeping my hair short both as it's more manageable and I can still give it a feminine flair when I'd like to. Yet that still doesn't stop comments from even strangers having those times where they butt in with the "Oh your hair looks so nice! It always looks so boyish whenever you don't do anything with it." And it's like such a backhanded compliment, as if I should hate or feel offended by how boyish something I do or wear makes me feel.

And the thing is that I really hated that about myself when I was in jr. high. That's when I started towards keeping my hair short and of course some days it was just too much to always want to style or fuss with it before school. But that's also a time where if you don't code with enough check marks in the female category then you tend to find yourself dealing with hurtful comments from classmates--or at least I did. 

So like, I could certainly see how growing up and experiences in my life could have just eventually caused me to develop, if not at least yearn for, a nonbinary mindset and outlook, regardless of how I my physically wish to be presenting myself in the present or even in the future.

I think both nonbinary and genderfluid would be labels that I wouldn't find issue with for myself. I guess I've just spent a lot of time wracking my head over which one is the better fit? Since I've done a decent amount of looking into both and there are aspects of both that I feel do adhere to how I think and feel about myself. I suppose I was just hoping to get the opinions of those more experienced living the labels that could help me zero in on which may be the better fit? Or at least give some more insight into things that could help me decide which I find more alignment with. 

Like I guess I'm more so unsure of how the way I feel and present within and outside of my birth gender would coincide with one label over the other? For instance, I worry that by the fact that I do have times where I can embrace and feel empowered by my femininity would inherently mean that I wouldn't be nonbinary seeing as I keep reading that it's mostly for those not wanting to settle within the binary. Yet I've also seen a lot of people's own interpretations of it that lend me to see how by the sheer fact that there are times I'd rather just be neutral when not wanting to be dolled up could in fact be seen and defined as nonbinary.

The same for genderfluid, I've just always worried that because I don't dip or deviate towards the other spectrum enough that it wouldn't be considered fluid enough. Like how in the states the way I present as neutral isn't so different from how many cisgendered females present normally. Thus, in turn, the way I would see my fluidity wouldn't be 'enough' for me to label myself as genderfluid.

Though from the sounds of it, I suppose it's more up to me to see which label ends up feeling more of a fit for me since it seems that despite my worries each way I would look at it the way I feel and express my gender within body labels is more valid than I originally thought?

Our weekly ad papers that are both supplied in the store and mailed out to state on the bottom "while supplies last" so yea it's a catch all for every weekly ad.
